title: Budget Spreadsheet Google Sheets and Excel, Monthly Budget Planner, Paycheck Budget, Expense Tracker, Bill and Debt Tracker for Beginners
description:
A simple monthly budget spreadsheet for Google Sheets and Excel, made for first-time and returning budgeters. Set up your money once, log what you spend each month, and see your whole year on one Dashboard.

What's inside: 19 tabs
- Start here: 5 short steps, a live Ready check and links to every month
- Dashboard: the year by month (income, spent, left over, saved and debt paid), your share to savings and debt, spending by category for the year, a bar chart by month and a pie chart by group (Needs, Wants, Savings, Debt)
- Setup: your income lines and up to 30 categories, each with a group and a monthly budget
- January to December: 12 month tabs, each with an 80-row spending log and budget vs actual for every category, with a progress bar that turns orange over 100% and the amount over shown in red
- Bills: due day, amount, autopay and a paid mark for each month
- Paycheck plan: every payday in the year, the bills due before the next one, and what is left from that paycheck
- Debt payoff: snowball or avalanche, your pay order, months and interest at the minimum, and an extra amount each month that goes to the first debt in pay order, with months with extra and interest saved
- Savings goals: a progress bar and how much to save each month to reach your date

The core is three tabs: Setup once, this month, Dashboard. Bills, Paycheck plan, Debt payoff and Savings goals are extras. Use them when you want them, skip them if you do not.

What makes it different
- A real file, not a link. You download the .xlsx workbook itself, so there is no view-only copy, no access to request, and your Etsy email does not have to match a Google account.
- A Ready check that tells you what is left. Each setup item shows Done or To do as you type: income entered, every dollar budgeted, every category grouped, spending that matches your categories, no amounts without a category, example cleared. Each To do says what to fix and where.
- See it work before you type. January comes filled in as an example month, so every total, bar and chart shows real numbers on first open, including one category over budget (Fun) shown in red. The example bills, debts and savings goals are there to show the math too. Clear or type over them when you are ready.
- Every dollar has a job. Setup shows Left to budget, and the Ready check shows your Needs, Wants and Savings plus debt split next to the 50/30/20 guide. It works for zero-based budgeting or 50/30/20.
- Budget by paycheck. Paid weekly, every 2 weeks or twice a month? The Paycheck plan lists every payday in the year, the bills due before the next one, and what is left. Paid monthly? You can skip this tab.
- Progress bars that look the same in both apps. The bars are made of filled blocks, so Google Sheets and Excel show the same thing.
- Hard to break. Shaded cells are for typing, plain cells calculate. Formulas are locked in Excel, color-coded in both. Rename a category in Setup and every month follows. The protection has no password, so you can still change anything. A savings goal shows Reached or Date passed: pick a new one, not an error.
- Start any month. Month tabs are not dated, and months with nothing logged stay out of your totals, so starting mid-year works. Starting in October, November or December? Set the Year in Setup to this year (2026) and use those months. In January, keep that copy as last year's record and start the new year in a fresh download, copying your Setup categories across.
- Instructions live inside the file: the Start here tab plus a one-line note at the top of every tab. There is no video.

Works with
- Google Sheets: upload the file to Google Drive, then open it with Google Sheets
- Excel 2019 or newer, Microsoft 365, and the free Excel for the web
- Set it up on a computer
Made for a personal or household budget in one currency. Amounts show in U.S. dollars ($); for another currency, unprotect the tab (no password) and change the number format.
Not for: Apple Numbers or LibreOffice (not tested), bank syncing or automatic imports, business bookkeeping.

How to start
1. Download the .xlsx from Etsy.com > Purchases on a computer and save it. Do not open it in a browser preview.
2. Open it. Google Sheets: on drive.google.com choose New > File upload, then open the file with Google Sheets. Excel: double-click the file.
3. Follow the Start here tab. It is the first tab, with 5 steps and the Ready check.

Questions buyers ask
Can I download it in the Etsy phone app?
No. The Etsy phone app cannot download files. Sign in at Etsy.com on a computer and go to Purchases.
The file opened in my browser and looks wrong. What now?
That is a browser preview, not the spreadsheet. Save the .xlsx to your computer first, then upload it to Google Drive and open it with Google Sheets, or double-click it to open in Excel.
Do I need to ask for access?
No. There is no link and no access request. The .xlsx is yours.

What you get
- Clear-Budget.xlsx (0.1 megabytes), one workbook with 19 tabs
Digital download. Nothing is shipped.

Help
Questions? Message us on Etsy.
